Today, we already connect two-thirds of all German hospitals with thousands of rehabilitation clinics, nursing and homecare providers. With around 100 employees, we continue to grow, and we’re looking for people with character who want to help us improve the healthcare system.


What you’ll do as our Tech Lead (Medical Coding Agents) (m/w/d):

German hospitals are paid a fixed amount per case, based on the codes assigned to it. Insurers dispute a share of the bills through an external medical audit, and the hospital can appeal when the audit cuts a bill. Recare is building medical coding agents to rebuild this chain: they read the case file, propose codes, assess audit findings and draft appeals. A subject matter expert reviews every result.

You’ll lead the technical development of this product. The role is about 80% hands-on building and 20% leading, and it grows with the platform into areas beyond billing.


  • Technical direction: set the architecture with the team across backend, frontend and a data model built on healthcare standards such as FHIR. Set the technical roadmap with the team and deliver on it predictably.

  • Agent orchestration: design how models, deterministic rules and human review fit together. Work with our AI engineers on system design.

  • Hands-on delivery: build the backend for cases, documents and long-running agent runs, including the append-only decision log that keeps every case audit-proof when an insurer challenges it months later.

  • Product partnership: be the technical counterpart to the product manager and the subject matter experts on planning, specs and trade-offs.

  • Production quality: own reliability, observability and security in a sensitive healthcare context, with an eval harness built from expert-reviewed cases as a CI gate.

How we work:

  • AI coding agents: engineers use them every day and take responsibility for the code we ship. Product managers and designers prototype in our codebase too, and engineers review what goes to production.

  • Human-in-the-loop: agents propose, the expert accepts, corrects or rejects, and every decision is logged with its evidence.

  • Shipping: we release early to development partners and switch features on per hospital.

  • Data protection: EU-only inference and no patient data in logs are hard constraints.

  • Ownership: product owns what we build and why. The tech lead owns how it’s built and that it ships.

  • Stack: TypeScript, Node.js and Go, Python for inference, Postgres, React, AWS Bedrock, Docker and Datadog.

  • Success: measured in revenue hospitals keep, not in usage.


What we’re looking for:

  • Leadership: 6+ years of experience, including leading a small team.

  • Hands-on with LLMs: you’ve built with LLMs yourself and understand where they fail: non-determinism, cost, latency and evaluation. You can design systems around them and challenge our AI engineers’ choices. Experience running an LLM or agent system in production is a strong plus, and strong personal projects count.

  • Evals: you can answer “how did you know it was good enough?” with ground truth, regression tests and a clear taxonomy of error classes.

  • Full-stack depth: you go deep across backend, frontend and data, and you commit code.

  • Other people’s systems: you’re comfortable with asynchronous pipelines, legacy interfaces and code written by others. Hospital experience isn’t required.

  • Communication: you explain decisions and trade-offs clearly in English in a remote team.

  • Nice to have: German, as the catalogues, the coding rules and much of the work with our experts are in German; an ML background, including judgement on when fine-tuning pays off; retrieval and source attribution; healthcare data standards such as FHIR; regulation such as MDR and the EU AI Act.

What we offer

  • Growth: we invest in each person’s development, whether that’s taking ownership of new projects, deepening your technical leadership or exploring new AI approaches, supported by a dedicated learning and development budget and regular feedback. If you grow, we grow.

  • Purposeful work: your work has a real impact on patients, their families and healthcare professionals.

  • Company culture: flat hierarchies, strong team dynamics and a culture of mutual respect, loyalty and recognition. English is our working language across a team of 20+ nationalities.

  • Flexibility: need to pick up your child from daycare or want to exercise at lunch? We support you, with fully remote work, flexible hours and workations by arrangement.

  • Your setup: a work laptop plus a one-off budget to choose and keep your own accessories.

  • Monthly benefit: €50 per month for vouchers or an Urban Sports Club membership (for employees in Germany).

  • Birthday off: your birthday off to celebrate with your loved ones.

  • Together: team meetups and company-wide events.

Location

We’re a remote team, and the role is fully remote within European time zones. We’re hiring in Germany, Austria, Spain, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

Your Role

As a (Junior) Graphic Designer in our Licensing Team at Statista R, you will work closely with Sales and Project Management to create effective, on-brand marketing and licensing materials. This is a great opportunity to build hands-on experience across print design, digital assets, brand implementation, and AI-supported design workflows.

 

Your Responsibilities

  • Design and develop sales and licensing materials, including brochures, cover letters, order forms, certificates, and presentation assets

  • Create premium quality seals and award badges that reflect the credibility and high standards of our rankings

  • Handle layout, final artwork, file preparation, and the creation of print-ready PDFs

  • Edit and optimize images for print and digital use

  • Improve and further develop existing sales collateral using innovative design methods and AI-powered creative tools

  • Design merchandise and promotional materials, such as stickers, roll-ups, and additional point-of-sale assets

  • Ensure all materials align with corporate design guidelines and maintain a consistent visual brand identity

  • Collaborate closely with Project Management and Sales to develop targeted, effective, and visually engaging sales communications

 

Your Profile

  • You have completed vocational training or hold a degree in Graphic Design, Media Design, Communication Design, or a comparable creative field

  • You have a strong eye for design, typography, composition, color, and detail

  • You enjoy developing creative concepts and translating ideas into clear, high-quality visual communication

  • You are proficient in the Adobe Creative Suite, particularly Adobe InDesign and Adobe Illustrator

  • You are curious about AI-based design tools and eager to explore how they can enhance creative workflows

  • You have initial experience with print products, prepress, print production, and corporate design implementation

  • You work in a structured, reliable, and organized way, with strong time-management skills

  • You communicate confidently in both German and English

What we offer

In addition to our great team, culture, and our shared goal of empowering people with data, there are many other things that make Statista a great place to work! Join us and benefit from:

  • Work from abroad up to 30 calendar days a year

  • Hybrid work and flex-time

  • International team and social events

  • Subsidized urban mobility and access to fitness and wellness options

  • Free access to Langdock and all its amazing functionalities

  • Career & training opportunities

  • Attractive locations and modern offices

  • Mental health support with OpenUp

Some of the benefits listed here apply only to the German entity and to Junior-level roles or above.

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Java/Kotlin (x/f/m)
description:
Senior Backend Engineer - Java/Kotlin (x/f/m)

Set a new pulse for healthcare!

We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the IAM (Identity and Access Management) team in Platform Services Tech.

Your mission will be to secure and scale the authentication capabilities that millions of Doctolib users rely on every day. You will drive the most impactful phases of a critical, multi-year migration to a self-hosted, Keycloak-based identity provider — a project at the intersection of platform engineering, security, and cross-team impact. Working in the tech team at Doctolib means building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the next phases of the multi-year authentication migration to a self-hosted, Keycloak-based identity provider — completing token-based sign-in for Doctolib Pro apps and making the identity provider the single source of truth for user data

  • Own the reliability of high-traffic authentication systems end-to-end: monitoring, alerting, SLOs, incident resolution, post-mortems, and safe rollout practices (feature flags, canary releases, zero-downtime migrations)

  • Drive cross-team delivery independently: produce design documents and decision memos, build alignment across dependent teams, and make trade-offs explicit

  • Collaborate closely with the Product Security team on security-sensitive architecture decisions and changes

  • Contribute to frontend development in React and TypeScript on the custom interfaces tied to the IAM platform

  • Use AI tools daily to accelerate your own work and help establish repeatable AI-augmented workflows across the team

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Have 7–10+ years of backend engineering experience with hands-on, daily Java or Kotlin development and a solid understanding of JVM internals (garbage collection, memory management, multi-threading, and profiling)

  • Have proven experience building and operating high-traffic production systems at scale — load testing, capacity planning, horizontal scaling, caching, and performance bottleneck identification

  • Own reliability end-to-end: you define monitoring, alerting, and SLOs, lead incident resolution, write post-mortems, and have shipped changes safely via feature flags, canary releases, and zero-downtime migrations on live systems

  • Have led complex, multi-week cross-team delivery independently — producing design docs, driving alignment across dependent teams, and making trade-offs explicit without waiting for consensus

  • Use AI tools daily in your engineering workflow, critically validate their outputs, and are excited to help establish shared AI practices for your team

  • Are fluent in English (written and spoken)

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have prior experience with identity providers (e.g. Keycloak), OAuth2, and/or OIDC

  • Have hands-on experience with security practices for exposed, high-traffic endpoints

  • Have contributed to frontend codebases in React and TypeScript

  • Have exposure to Kafka/CDC

  • Have exposure to mobile authentication

Life at Doctolib Tech

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack is composed of Rails, TypeScript, Java, Python, Kotlin, Swift, and React Native.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here.

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site.

What we offer

  • A Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass) fully paid for by Doctolib

  • 28 vacation days + 1 additional day for each full calendar year of employment (up to a maximum of 30 days)

  • Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

  • Company health insurance with great supplementary benefits through our partner Allianz

  • Company pension scheme (bAV) through Allianz with an employer subsidy of 40% (15% within the probationary period)

  • The Doctolib Parent Care program, which includes one month additional parental leave and much more

  • Enrollment in Doctolib's long-term employee value sharing plan called DoctoGrowth

  • Free mental health and coaching services through our partner Moka.care

  • Subsidized sports membership through our partner Urban Sports Club

  • A flexible workplace policy offering both hybrid and office-based mode

  • Alongside healthy snacks and our regular breakfast buffet, we provide a subsidized meal benefit

  • For caregivers and workers with disabilities, a package including an adaptation of the remote policy, extra days off for medical reasons, and psychological support

  • Access to the best AI tools for coding, development and dedicated training

Our interview process

  • TA Screen

  • Coding interview

  • System Design Interview

  • Behavioural Peer Interview

We want your experience to be clear, respectful, and transparent. Learn more about our hiring process on our candidate experience page.

Job details

  • Permanent position

  • Full-time

  • Berlin, Germany

  • Hybrid work setup (up to 2 remote days per week)

  • Start date: as soon as possible

We welcome everyone

At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. This translates into our recruitment process. We evaluate candidates based solely on qualifications and motivation, without any form of discrimination.

The more diverse ideas are heard, the more our product will truly improve healthcare for all. You are welcome to apply to Doctolib, regardless of your gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or disability.

To ensure equal opportunities, we invite you to exclude personal information (e.g., pictures, age) from your applications. If you require any accommodation, please let us know for support during the hiring process.

Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of!

All information provided is processed by Doctolib for application management. For data processing details, click here: France. Please contact hr.dataprivacy(at)doctolib.com for inquiries or to exercise your rights.

description:
Trust unlocks our greatest potential.

For decades, the clearing of payments remained unchanged and unchallenged. We asked, what if there was a better way? What if we could make banking infrastructure faster, safer, more reliable, and easier to access for all? Here is where you can think radically and responsibly to find the best solution.

What happens when you know you’re inherently trusted? Trust creates safety. Safety encourages you to be brave, to challenge, to fail, to try new things and to execute. At ClearBank everything revolves around trust. We’re not expected to earn it, but we are expected not to break it. We’re trusted to own it. To solve issues in the moment. To know a good risk when we see one, and the judgement to know that ‘can’ doesn’t always mean you ‘should’

What you can expect:

ClearBank is a place where you can do things differently and challenge the status quo. We will give you a high level of autonomy and transparency, and we trust you to make the right decisions for the bank.

If that excites you, how about joining our Client Services team as a Client Complaint Senior Analyst? Reporting to the Associate Director, Client Support you will take independent ownership of client complaints, using your judgement and complaints expertise to resolve non-routine cases fairly, effectively and within relevant requirements. You will support consistently high standards across complaint handling by identifying themes and improvements, sharing your knowledge and providing direct line management, day-to-day support and coaching to the Complaint Analyst.

Your role includes:

  • Independently manage client complaints from receipt through to resolution, applying sound judgement to deliver fair, timely and well-evidenced outcomes in line with complaint handling standards, relevant requirements and internal policies

  • Investigate non-routine complaints, bringing together information from systems, teams and stakeholders to establish root cause, reach appropriate conclusions and identify when complex matters require escalation

  • Produce clear, accurate and customer-focused written responses, ensuring decisions and outcomes are appropriately supported and communicated

  • Identify recurring complaint themes, risks and root causes, using insight from cases to suggest practical improvements to customer outcomes, service quality and complaint management processes

  • Take direct line management responsibility for the Client Complaint Analyst, setting clear objectives, holding regular one-to-ones, providing feedback and coaching, and supporting their onboarding, performance and development

  • Share complaints knowledge and best practice across the team while continuing to manage your own complaint caseload

  • Support consistent complaint handling standards across the team by providing guidance on day-to-day cases and constructively challenging where an approach may not achieve the right outcome

  • Build trusted relationships across Client Services, Financial Crime, Operations, Product and other relevant teams to resolve issues and support improvements that benefit customers and the Bank

What you’ll bring:

To excel in this role, you’ll also need:

  • Strong working knowledge of complaint handling in a customer service, financial services, operations or regulated environment, with the ability to apply relevant processes, policies and controls independently

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, including the ability to investigate non-routine issues, assess evidence, identify root causes and reach well-reasoned conclusions

  • Sound judgement, with the confidence to make day-to-day decisions independently and recognise when a more complex or higher-risk matter should be escalated

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex matters clearly and produce high-quality customer communications

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage varied complaint activity and competing priorities while maintaining quality and timeliness

  • A collaborative approach, with the ability to line manage the Complaints Analysts, set clear expectations, provide constructive feedback and coaching, and support their performance and development

  • Curiosity and a continuous-improvement mindset, with the confidence to identify problems, challenge constructively and suggest better ways of working

What makes a great ClearBank team member? Does this sound like you?

  • You focus on solutions and positive outcomes, thinking radically and responsibly to find the best result for our customers, your colleagues and the bank;

  • You actively seek feedback from others to drive your growth and development, always assuming positive intent from others and develop strong, trusting relationships you’re your colleagues and customers: you really, genuinely care;

  • You always strive for the highest quality, but you know that done is better than perfect; you welcome a challenge knowing that they learn as you go and iterate;

  • ‘I’ before ’we’, isn’t in your vocabulary.

Regretfully we are not able to sponsor applicants for immigration purposes at the current time.

What we offer in return:

  • We're flexible – We support a culture of flexibility which allows our employees to achieve a strong work-life balance.

  • Offices – Work in a way that works for you – whether that’s in the London office, at home, or hybrid.

  • Holiday – 27 days of annual leave per year, plus bank holidays.

  • Holiday buy/sell - Buy or sell up to five days of annual leave each year and shape your year around what matters most.

  • Work abroad – You have the flexibility to work outside of the UK for up to 30 days in a rolling 12-month period.

  • Socials – Regular social events open to all.

  • Holiday swap – Option to swap your bank holidays to any other day of your choice.

  • Wellbeing – 24/7 employee assistance programme including mental health support, life assurance and income protection.

  • Bigger than ClearBank – Take a couple of days per year to do something that matters to you.

  • Healthy living – Private healthcare and discounted dental cover, with employee perks and discounts.

  • Family – Enhanced family-friendly leave.

  • Personal development – We offer personal development budgets, opportunities to take part in role-related training and unlimited LinkedIn Learning.

And not forgetting the biggest benefit of all. The opportunity to be part of an incredible team that’s building a tech-bank fit for the future.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

  • 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

  • Our enhanced family leave policies

  • Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

  • Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.  

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time.  

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully.  

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon!  

Equal Opportunities

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation.

In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. 

The legal bit

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. description:
People Analytics Analyst

About Us

ClearBank is a technology-enabled bank built to help transform banking and payments. We combine banking expertise and technology to provide infrastructure that enables our clients to deliver innovative financial products and services. Our culture is founded on trust, accountability, learning, collaboration and the confidence to challenge established ways of working responsibly.

We built ClearBank on the belief that banking infrastructure would no longer slow down progress. Instead, it would be a catalyst that unlocks the potential to innovate. It would adapt to different needs so a new era in financial services could begin. We’re here to challenge the status quo in banking, are you?

We all know that transforming banking forever is not an easy mission, but we’re more than ready to rise to that challenge. We all do it every day; navigating new, unexpected and sometimes even daunting challenges. But we believe in ourselves and trust we can do it. Want to innovate? Go for it. Push for a better way? You Can. If you think you have it in you, this is Where You Can.

The role:

Reporting to our Head of People, as the People Analytics Analyst you will help the People Team make informed, evidence-led decisions by turning data into clear, accurate and actionable insight.

Working across the People Team you will deliver reporting and analysis that supports organisational effectiveness, particularly focusing on Reward and People Operations among the wider team.

You will strengthen data quality, reporting controls and analytical capability across the People function, making insight easier to understand and use while protecting the confidentiality of employee information.

Key Responsibilities

  • Produce regular and ad hoc people reporting that gives stakeholders a clear view of workforce trends, risks and opportunities.

  • Analyse data across the employee lifecycle, including workforce composition, recruitment, retention, progression, performance, absence, engagement and inclusion.

  • Develop accessible dashboards, reports and visualisations that turn complex data into clear insights for People and business stakeholders.

  • Partner with Reward to support pay benchmarking, reward reviews, pay-positioning analysis and other compensation-related activity through accurate data preparation and analysis.

  • Maintain accurate and consistent people datasets, including clear data definitions, validation checks, reconciliation, documentation and version control.

  • Investigate data anomalies and work with People, Finance, Payroll and other stakeholders to resolve root causes and improve source-data quality.

  • Support workforce planning and organisational analysis by identifying patterns, modelling scenarios and presenting evidence-based observations.

  • Provide analytical support for People projects and recurring processes, ensuring outputs are accurate, timely and appropriate for their intended audience.

  • Improve reporting processes through automation, standardisation and the reduction of unnecessary manual activity.

  • Promote responsible use of people data by applying appropriate confidentiality, access, governance and quality controls.

What success looks like in the role:

  • Stakeholders receive accurate, timely and decision-ready people insights that help them understand workforce priorities and take appropriate action.

  • Core People reporting is supported by clear definitions, effective controls and reliable data that stakeholders trust.

  • People analytics increasingly covers the wider employee lifecycle, while Reward receives consistent and high-quality analytical support.

  • Recurring reports and processes become more efficient, scalable and easier to use through thoughtful automation and standardisation.

  • Complex findings are communicated clearly, with appropriate context, enabling stakeholders to understand both the evidence and its limitations.

Skills & Experience:

  • Experience in people analytics, HR reporting, workforce analytics, business analysis or another data-focused role.

  • Strong analytical and numerical skills, including experience working with detailed or complex datasets.

  • Ability to translate analysis into concise insights, clear visual outputs and practical recommendations.

  • Strong Excel / Databricks capability, including formulas, data validation, reconciliation, data manipulation and structured analysis. Use or advocacy of AI is welcome.

  • Experience producing recurring reports, dashboards or management information for different stakeholder groups.

  • Strong attention to detail and a consistent approach to checking, documenting and controlling analytical outputs.

  • Understanding of data quality, confidentiality and the responsible handling of sensitive employee information.

  • Ability to investigate anomalies, identify root causes and work collaboratively with others to resolve data issues.

  • Strong planning and organisational skills, with the ability to manage recurring reporting alongside ad hoc analytical requests.

  • Clear communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings to non-technical audiences.

Nice-to-have

  • Experience working within a People or HR function in a regulated organisation, financial-services business or technology company.

  • Familiarity with HR information systems, reporting platforms or data-visualisation tools. Notable; Databricks.

  • Experience supporting workforce planning, organisational design, employee-listening or inclusion analysis.

  • Exposure to reward analytics, salary benchmarking, pay-review modelling or compensation data.

  • Experience improving or automating reporting and data processes.

Ways of Working & Culture

  • Care like we mean it: Handle people data with care, respect and discretion, while producing insight that considers its impact on colleagues and the organisation.

  • Build trust together: Take ownership of data quality and delivery, follow through on commitments, exercise sound judgement and raise risks or limitations early.

  • Grow with the challenge: Stay curious, seek feedback and build analytical capability while adapting to changing priorities and new questions.

  • Succeed as one: Work collaboratively across People, Reward, Finance, Payroll and the wider business, engaging stakeholders early and focusing on shared outcomes.

  • Clear a bold new path: Challenge inefficient reporting practices, test better approaches and build solutions that can scale as the organisation’s analytical needs evolve.

Role Level: 2

title: Product Manager
description:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Core Experience Team 👋
The Core Experience team looks after how our customers find and book rail travel across the UK and Europe. Our work covers search, supply from carriers and the booking experience, all in service of our purpose of empowering greener travel choices and connecting people and places. We are a collaborative group who enjoy learning from our customers and from each other.

This is a brand new role, created to own what happens once a customer has found the right journey and moves towards booking: reservation details, optional extras and payment. Because it sits so close to the point of purchase, it offers a direct line to customer experience and revenue, and plenty of room to grow. You will work alongside our Search team and the Supply and Payments platform teams, with colleagues in commercial, design, data and engineering, to make booking simple and reliable for customers in every market we serve.

In this role as the Product Manager, Booking Conversion, you will...🚄

  • Own the customer experience from the moment someone chooses a journey to a confirmed booking, setting clear goals for conversion (the share of customers who complete their booking) and revenue while enabling other teams with a stake in the journey.

  • Run quick cycles of experimentation by forming hypotheses, testing ideas, learning from the results and iterating, while shaping a longer-term vision and roadmap for the booking journey.

  • Use customer insight and data to understand where people hesitate or leave, and decide where to invest limited team capacity across each step of the journey.

  • Build a deep understanding of how rail works in different markets and with different carriers. Decide when a market or carrier specific improvement is the right investment, and when to bring ideas and learnings together across markets so that value grows for customers everywhere, rather than staying in one place.

  • Balance wider business goals from other teams, such as adding new supply, increasing booking features for each carrier, and introducing optional extras and new revenue streams, against keeping the journey simple and low in friction for customers.

  • Partner closely with the Supply, Search, New Business, and Payments platform teams, alongside design, data and engineering, to align priorities and deliver improvements together.

  • Communicate openly with a wide range of stakeholders, including commercial colleagues, explaining the reasoning behind decisions and sharing progress and results in a way that builds trust.

  • Bring AI tools into your everyday work, such as prototyping, analysis and delivery, and help the team grow in confidence using them.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Experience improving conversion in a digital booking, checkout or purchase journey, using data to spot opportunities and measure the impact of your changes.

  • Hands-on experience designing and running experiments, and turning what you learn into the next set of improvements.

  • A customer-first mindset, with the ability to combine customer insight and data to make confident decisions even when information is incomplete.

  • Confidence setting direction for a product area, balancing near-term improvements with a longer-term vision.

  • Clear, thoughtful communication, with the ability to explain complex trade-offs and build alignment between teams who may have different priorities.

  • Comfort weighing limited capacity against competing demands, and explaining what you will focus on and why.

  • Ideally, experience balancing local needs with a wider shared strategy, for example across several markets or with third-party suppliers. It is also helpful if you are familiar with travel, ticketing or payments.

  • You may also be curious about AI tools and keen to use them to prototype ideas, analyse results and speed up delivery.

description:
About Keyrock

Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 200+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris and New York.

We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.

 

We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.

What we are looking for

We are seeking a Head of Risk to own and develop the Firm’s risk function end-to-end. This is a senior leadership role with direct accountability for the design, implementation and enforcement of a Firm-wide risk framework across all activities.

The role requires strong quantitative risk expertise and the ability to apply rigorous methodologies to complex, real-time markets across both traditional finance and digital assets. The successful candidate will co-design the firm’s risk architecture with the COO and CIO, covering data, analytics and real-time risk aggregation.

You will have full oversight of risk across trading (spot and derivatives), treasury and investments, including exposures across CeFi and DeFi environments. This includes defining risk appetite, implementing advanced risk metrics and ensuring disciplined risk-taking across the organization.

We are looking for a leader who sets the standard, challenges the business and enforces a strong risk culture, while enabling the firm to scale.

 
 

Role description

Quantitative Risk Framework: Develop and maintain a quantitative risk framework grounded in modern risk theory (e.g. market, credit, liquidity and systemic risk modelling), leveraging concepts such as tail risk, extreme value theory, dependence structures and stress testing

Firm-wide Risk System Architecture: Co-design and implement the Firm-wide risk management system in close collaboration with the COO and CIO, including data architecture, risk aggregation layers, real-time monitoring capabilities and reporting infrastructure across all business lines.

Cross-Asset & Cross-Infrastructure Risk Integration: Build an integrated risk view across centralized and decentralized venues, covering exchange risk, counterparty risk, smart contract risk, collateral efficiency and liquidity fragmentation.

Advanced Risk Modelling & Metrics: Define and implement advanced risk metrics (VaR, Expected Shortfall, stress scenarios, liquidity-adjusted risk, concentration risk) and ensure their consistent application across trading, treasury and investment activities.

Is plus: TradFi ↔ Crypto Risk Translation: Translate traditional financial risk methodologies into crypto-native environments, adapting models to account for 24/7 markets, fragmented liquidity, funding dynamics, on-chain transparency and new failure modes (e.g. oracle risk, protocol risk).

 
 

Background and Experience

Quantitative Risk Expertise: Strong foundation in quantitative risk management, including hands-on experience with market risk, credit risk and liquidity risk modelling, ideally aligned with frameworks such as those presented in Quantitative Risk Management (McNeil, Frey, Embrechts).

Modelling & Analytical Skills: Demonstrated ability to design and implement risk models, including tail risk estimation, scenario analysis, stress testing frameworks and dependence modelling across asset classes.

System Design & Cross-Functional Leadership: Proven experience in designing or co-designing firm-wide risk systems, working closely with technology (CIO) and operations (COO) to translate risk requirements into scalable infrastructure.

TradFi + Crypto Hybrid Experience: Experience operating at the intersection of traditional financial markets and digital assets (CeFi and/or DeFi), with a strong understanding of differences in market structure, risk transmission and infrastructure.

Crypto-Specific Risk Understanding: Practical knowledge of crypto-specific risks, including exchange/custodian risk, smart contract risk, protocol risk, funding/basis dynamics and collateral management in both centralized and decentralized environments.

Competences and personality

  • Strong drive and proactivity to continuously strengthen the risk management in a fast-growing financial institution

  • The candidate reports to the COO but this is not a reporting role, but a quantitative risk management system-building role.

Our recruitment philosophy


We look for self-aware candidates who bring both the core skills required for the role and a deep alignment with our performance principles. We seek fiercely passionate, mission-driven people who communicate with purpose and practice proactive ownership. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who prioritizes mission over ego, maintains a commercial mindset, and delivers long-term value through pragmatic flexibility.

title: Finance Manager
description:
We're Heidi.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

Heidi's UK and Europe business is growing faster than the finance scaffolding underneath it. Central finance across Sydney, Melbourne and Manila runs month-end close, core accounting and day-to-day operations, but the region needs someone on the ground who owns the accuracy of its numbers and sits close enough to the commercial team to shape decisions before they get made. Today, regional leaders wait on Australian hours for answers about their own P&L. You'll end that.

The role has two halves and both carry equal weight. You'll own regional financial control and compliance: the integrity of the balance sheet, the accuracy of management reporting and forecasts, cash, strong local controls, and statutory obligations across Companies House, HMRC and VAT, directed through external advisers. You'll also be a hands-on business partner to UK and Europe leadership, Sales and Customer Success, owning the P&L narrative, bringing a commercial view to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, and making sure teams see the financial consequence of the choices they make. You'll report to the Group Financial Controller with a dotted line to FP&A.

What you'll do

Financial reporting and month-end close

  • Own the integrity of the UK&Europe balance sheet, with reconciliations that stay current, reviewed and explainable

  • Own the accuracy of the UK&Europe monthly group reporting and management accounts with variance commentary that explains movements

  • Be the single point of contact for group finance on anything UK&Europe: queries, adjustments, restatements, consolidation-level questions

Compliance and risk oversight

  • Own the UK&Europe compliance calendar (Companies House, HMRC, VAT) by directing external accountants and advisers

  • Own the adviser relationships (accounting, tax, audit), keeping work well scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi's internal finance standards

  • Build an early-warning process so compliance risk is caught and escalated well before it threatens trading status

  • Be the accountable owner if something in the compliance chain breaks down

Commercial business partnering

  • Be the day-to-day finance partner to UK&Europe leadership, owning the regional P&L narrative, budget vs actual and the "why" behind the numbers

  • Bring a commercial lens to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, flagging risk and opportunity early

  • Translate regional performance into clear, decision-ready input for FP&A and company leadership

  • Give UK&Europe business leaders a reliable, self-serve view of their numbers, so decisions stop waiting on Australian hours

  • Feed central finance the regional inputs it needs at close: accrual estimates, revenue and spend context, then review and sign off on the UK&Europe result

Revenue risk and collections

  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success to resolve aged and disputed balances and unblock stuck revenue

  • Own the commercial view of collection risk: which accounts, why, and what it means for cash, and feed it into forecasting

  • Drive down UK&Europe DSO by fixing the upstream causes (contracting, disputes, process), not by chasing invoices

FinOps, controls and performance frameworks

  • Build the operating rhythm that turns UK&Europe finance from reactive support into a reliable performance framework: clear KPIs, owners, review cadences and escalation paths

  • Partner with budget owners on spend decisions before they are made, rather than policing them after the fact

  • Strengthen financial controls across spend, approvals, vendor onboarding, card usage, subscriptions and commercial commitments, while keeping the process pragmatic for a fast-moving region

  • Review regional AP and card activity, including prompt removal of leaver access and cards, and escalate anomalies to central finance operations

  • Partner with external accountants, tax advisers, compliance providers and other vendors, making sure work is well-scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi’s internal finance standards

  • Use FinOps-style discipline to connect spend, usage and outcomes, especially across tooling, GTM systems, implementation costs and region-specific operating expenses

  • Create simple documentation and control checks so the region can scale without relying on informal knowledge or one-off fixes

What you'll need

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen — comfortable moving between P&L narrative, deal economics and cash impact

  • Experience business partnering with Sales, Customer Success or regional leadership in a growth business

  • Track record improving collections or DSO by fixing root causes, not just process

  • Experience owning spend or expense controls in a way that supports the business rather than only governing it

  • Comfortable directing (not necessarily performing) statutory compliance and VAT work through external advisers

  • High degree of autonomy and ownership in a small, remote-first global finance team

  • Clear, confident communicator — able to hold your own with commercial leaders and external advisers alike

  • Experience in a multi-entity or multi-currency business

Nice to have

  • Experience in a high-growth SaaS or technology company

  • Qualified accountant (ACA / ACCA / CIMA or equivalent)

  • Exposure to Companies House, HMRC and Irish Revenue processes

  • Experience with Campfire, Airwallex or similar modern finance tooling

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You'll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we'd like to see. We're medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who've felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we're building isn't always easy. But we didn't choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn't whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you're doing the defining work of your career.

We take care of you.

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

title: Director, Satellite Business International | Directeur(trice), Développement Commercial International - Satellites
CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description:
The question

Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards.

What you will do

The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request.

1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report.

2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured.

3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along.

4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements.

A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.


Who we are looking for Required

• A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract.

• A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models.

• Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure.

• Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI.

• Working English; French is not required.

Valued, not required

Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.

What matters most

We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.

What we offer

• A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot.

• A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design.

• Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI).

• Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers.

• Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling.

Conditions

Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment.

description:
TL;DR Davis is hiring a Founding Data Researcher to build the data behind our foundation model, trained from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. You will own the data end to end, from raw floorplans and synthetic generation to a canonical representation, curation, large-scale pretraining and the ablations that tell us which data actually moves the model. Here the dataset is part of the algorithm.

About Davis

Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate four to five fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they will need only one: Davis.

We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.

We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

The Role

You will own the data our foundation model learns from, a model we train from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. Part of the corpus comes from real floorplans as images and PDFs that have to become clean, standardized graphs. A large part will be synthetic, procedurally generated building graphs, geometry and rendered floorplans, with controlled variation in style, scan noise, annotations and furniture, each kept with its ground-truth graph automatically.

You will think about the whole loop, from raw and synthetic data to a canonical structured representation, curation and validation, the training dataset, large-scale pretraining, evaluation, data ablations, and back to improving the generator and the data mixture. You are senior enough to architect the data stack and set the data strategy, and hands-on enough to write the pipelines, run the experiments, train the models and do the ablations yourself.

What you will be working on

  • Corpus from raw sources. Turn real floorplans (images, PDFs, scans) into clean, standardized building graphs, with the geometry and semantics that make them trainable.

  • Synthetic data generation. Explore strategies to expand the dataset with synthetic data.

  • Canonical representation and curation. Define the standardized representation, then filter, deduplicate, quality-score and validate at scale, with versioning, provenance and lineage.

  • Pretraining data and mixtures. Assemble the training datasets, design the mixture and the curriculum, and blend synthetic and real data for large-scale pretraining.

  • Data ablations. Train models to learn which data actually helps, read the results, and feed them back into the generator and the mixture.

  • Evaluation. Build the eval harness (datasets, metrics, regression tests, monitoring) that tracks data and model quality over time.

What We Are Looking For

  • You have built the dataset, not just trained on it. You have personally built or generated the data used for a large pretraining run, from raw or synthetic sources, rather than only training on a dataset someone handed you.

  • Senior and deeply hands-on. At least 5 years of strong experience, senior enough to architect the data stack and set strategy, but still coding the pipelines, running the experiments and doing the ablations yourself.

  • Data as a first-class problem. A track record where the data itself is the object: curation, filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixtures, synthetic generation.

  • Strong engineering. Deep Python, clean and typed code, async and concurrency, distributed data pipelines, TDD culture.

Nice to have

  • Computer vision and document understanding, images to structured output, OCR, layout extraction, segmentation, geometry extraction, vectorization, raster to vector, image to scene graph, 3D or CAD.

  • Graph and structured scientific data, molecular, protein or scene graphs, meshes, CAD, BIM, 3D geometry, or relational and structured world data.

  • Synthetic worlds and simulation, a structured state to a simulator to a renderer to synthetic images with perfect labels, then a perception model, with an eye on the sim-to-real gap.

  • Foundation models from scratch, real involvement in a large pretraining run, not only fine-tuning.

  • Public evidence of data ownership, lead on a dataset, a Hugging Face release, a dataset card, a technical blog on your pipeline, or a talk on data curation or synthetic data.

  • GIS and geometry, parcels, zoning layers, projections, computational geometry or constrained optimization.

  • Multi-country data, heterogeneous sources, localization and varying rules.

Why Join Davis

  • Own the data end to end, from the generator to the pretraining mixture, as the person who defines what the model learns from.

  • Shape a foundation model from scratch, on a structured representation no one else is training on.

  • Work on genuinely hard problems, image to graph, synthetic worlds and large-scale pretraining, with your work reaching clients within days.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity, at a founding level, in an early-stage company.

  • Join a world-class team, a mix of AI researchers, engineers and architects backed by world-class VCs.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we're going after:

Team

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He is a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we are a team of twelve: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise. We are small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you are the one we need.

Why We Will Win

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It did not work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We do not sell tools, we sell the work, AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability, and parametric tools only check constraints after generation, which leaves designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this, but does not yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. These layouts may look plausible yet break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they are usable.

This is exactly the gap Davis closes. Because our model generates on structured representations rather than pixels, it produces compliant, editable plans from the start, and the data you build feeds that model directly.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you are drawn to what we are building but do not meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet all of the criteria. If that is you, please do not let it hold you back. We would love to receive your application.

title: AI Engineer
description:
Alassio recherche son (sa) prochain(e) AI Engineer !

 
 

Missions

 

🏗️ Alassio en quelques mots

En France, la paie et le social comptent parmi les fonctions les plus réglementées qui soient. Entre inflation réglementaire et évolutions légales et conventionnelles incessantes, la conformité est devenue un véritable fardeau pour les cabinets de paie et les services RH :

  • ce fardeau les empêche de se consacrer à ce qui compte vraiment, le conseil et l'accompagnement des salariés, qui en subissent donc eux aussi le poids

  • c'est aussi l'un des métiers où l'attrition est la plus forte en France, notamment parce que 60 % du temps des gestionnaires de paie est encore consacré à de la saisie ou à de la relecture manuelle

Pourtant, des solutions technologiques majeures existent : l'IA permet en particulier d'automatiser une très grande partie des tâches les plus pénibles et de valoriser les données sociales. Mais le secteur reste largement à l'écart de cette révolution, et le problème n'est pas seulement réglementaire : le marché était verrouillé par des éditeurs historiques vieillissants, difficiles à quitter faute d'alternative crédible et de moyens pour migrer efficacement. Là aussi, l'IA fait voler ces barrières en éclats et ouvre la voie à une vague d'innovation attendue depuis des décennies.

C'est pour y répondre qu'Alassio construit la plateforme de paie et de gestion RH moderne qui manquait à ce marché, au service des cabinets et de leurs clients TPE/PME. Notre ambition est de développer en un temps record :

  • une plateforme collaborative et ouverte, qui s'intègre nativement aux outils des cabinets et de leurs clients, respecte leurs habitudes de travail et fluidifie les échanges entre gestionnaires de paie et entreprises

  • l'automatisation de la tenue administrative : collecte des données, paramétrage des évolutions légales et des règles propres à chaque entreprise, génération automatique des rapports et formulaires, traçabilité juridique dynamique et en temps réel, etc.

  • la valorisation des données de paie et sociales, pour offrir un conseil social à 360° et enfin répondre efficacement à l'ensemble des attentes des salariés, qui se sont de surcroît largement amplifiées depuis le Covid : gestion contractuelle, pilotage de la masse salariale, avantages salariés, fidélisation des talents, mutuelle…

L'objectif : devenir le « People OS » sur lequel les cabinets et leurs clients TPE/PME s'appuient pour gérer l'intégralité de leurs problématiques paie et RH.

 

🚀 Tes responsabilités

Ta mission : faire de l'IA le levier qui démultiplie le travail de chacun chez Alassio. L'objectif est assumé : multiplier par 10 la productivité de chaque membre de l'équipe.

  • Tu formes la Growth squad avec notre Founding Strategy & Operations : ce binôme transverse optimise l'existant, automatise les workflows de toutes les équipes et fait passer nos initiatives IA et nos outils internes à l'échelle : hébergement et mise en production dans des environnements partagés, sécurité, observabilité, optimisation et amélioration continue

  • Tu deviens le (la) référent(e) IA d'Alassio : on se veut profondément AI-native et on expérimente énormément. Tu centralises et coordonnes ces initiatives pour que ce "lab interne" soit efficace, et tu expérimentes aussi en continu avec toutes les techno IA (budget et outillage conséquents)

  • Tu construis la nouvelle colonne vertébrale IT d'Alassio, en identifiant les systèmes IA qui comptent à l'échelle de toute l'entreprise

  • Tu prépares l'avenir du produit : à terme, les usages testés et éprouvés en interne sous ton impulsion ont vocation à rejoindre notre plateforme. Ils nourriront le « People OS » qui démocratise les cas d'usage les plus pertinents de l'IA dans notre secteur

 

🧭 Tes premiers chantiers

Ton point de départ : Bedrock, notre OS interne. Un peu à la manière de Palantir Foundry, il agrège & orchestre tout le contexte de l'entreprise pour en tirer des actions concrètes : suivi ultra-personnalisé et automatisé de nos utilisateurs, analyse produit, documentation, rédaction de tickets et PR associées…

Bedrock est déjà au cœur du quotidien de toutes les équipes. Mais il s'est construit par couches successives, au fil des cas d'usage ajoutés. Ton premier objectif est d'en dresser l'inventaire complet, process et outils IA compris. Tu définis ensuite la roadmap qui le fera changer de dimension :

  • Workflows : optimiser l'existant

  • Infrastructure : sécurité, confidentialité, hébergement et environnements partagés, pour un OS multi-joueur, plug-and-play et scalable

  • Observabilité : suivre les agents et leur performance, et améliorer chaque logique en continu

  • Autonomie : construire des workflows agentiques déclenchés par webhook ou planifiés, qui nettoient le contexte et mènent des missions 24/7

Très vite, tu as vocation à devenir le (la) responsable qui orchestre l'IA chez Alassio, et le (la) référent(e) de notre OS Bedrock.

 
 

Profil recherché

 

🌱 Expérience

  • 1 à 2 ans d'expérience dans un rôle d'AI Engineer / FDE / AI Deployment Strategist dans une top structure tech (BCGX, Palantir, Dust)

  • Plusieurs missions concrètes de déploiement et d'optimisation de technologies IA : mise en place de zéro d'un workflow au sein d'une organisation, sujets de gouvernance et de déploiement en entreprise, etc.

  • Une utilisation intensive des outils IA et une bonne maîtrise de Python : Claude Code / Codex ; Cursor Agents, Linear/PostHog, déploiement et hébergement (cloud, AI routers, etc.)

 

💎 Qualités

  • Un goût pour l'optimisation et l'organisation : tu aimes que les choses soient claires, que l'information soit facile à mobiliser, propre et maintenable, et tu prends plaisir à produire vite des éléments actionnables

  • Un biais très fort pour l'action : tu repères les problèmes avant qu'on te les signale, et tu ne t'arrêtes jamais au diagnostic

  • Penser à l'échelle : tu conçois dès le départ des solutions capables d'encaisser des montées en charge ×10 ou ×100, tout en restant pragmatique sur ce qui compte à court et moyen terme

 
 

Processus de sélection

  1. Premier entretien avec Tancrède (CEO) : 45 min

  2. Étude de cas technique avec Hector (COO) et Ivan Robert (Founding SWE) : 1h30

  3. Rencontre informelle de l'équipe dans nos bureaux, puis échange de 45 min avec les fondateurs Ayoub (CAIO), Paul (CTO), Tancrède (CEO) & Hector (COO)

  4. Deux à trois prises de référence

 
 

Ce que nous offrons

 

👊 Une mission unique

Tu rejoins une aventure entrepreneuriale en plein passage à l'échelle, sur un marché verrouillé depuis des années. On est convaincus que l'IA ne transformera pas seulement le produit et secteur qu'on construit, mais aussi la façon avec laquelle toutes les entreprises devront se réinventer. On en fait déjà l'expérience au quotidien avec Bedrock, notre OS interne qui est aujourd'hui au cœur de l'activité de toutes nos équipes tech et non-tech.

Ton rôle est de faire passer ce laboratoire à l'échelle pour que chaque équipe d'Alassio aille plus vite, avec l'ambition assumée de bâtir une référence en matière d'organisation AI-native.

 

🎁 Rémunération et avantages
